lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer at Gowans (AUD, premium extra); no UNSOLD or ASKING entries found. Close entries run $10 (plain green-cabochon bar brooch) to $80-85 (bolder malachite plaque and figural deco brooch). For context I re-ran the API: 121 past Gowans sterling silver brooch lots sold $5 to $140 hammer, median $35, middle half $20 to $55; the $125-140 ones were hallmarked and dated.
lots.working: No surviving SOLD entry is the same item (a stepped deco bar with a cabochon), so by the rules keep and flip are 0. For reference only: the lowest close sale ($10) would give keep 10/1.198 = $8 -> $5, and the best close sales ($80-85) would give about $65. A sensible personal ceiling if you like it is around $35-45 hammer (median plain 925 brooch $35). Flip: resale about $40-60 less about 10% selling fee and $10 post = $26-44, /2.396 = $10-18, so there is no flip margin.
lots.confidence_reason: 925 mark read in photo 2, but no same-item SOLD comparison; close comps span $10 to $85; stone type and age unconfirmed.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's aggregate 'Range $5 to $140 across about 100 lots, aud_price 40' entry: it is a category summary, not a single sale, so it cannot be an entry (my own re-run of the figures is in guide_summary). All seven single Gowans entries were checked in the API (id, title, sale_price, bid count and listing date all match) and kept, with photos of the three close ones viewed. Re-classed 430520 and 370142 as close rather than near-identical: one is a much bolder plaque, one figural.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: six graduated rails stepped down to a short bottom bar, round bright green translucent cabochon in an open C-shaped collet, about 5-6cm wide. Photo 2: back stamped 925 clearly, no maker mark, no hallmarks, pin and catch present. Heavy tarnish and some dark residue on the back.
lots.condition: Appears complete with stone intact and pin present; tarnished on the back; no obvious bends in the rails from the photo. Stone not tested.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any maker mark besides 925 (for example a German or Danish maker), does the pin close firmly in the catch, and is the stone loose or chipped?

lots.guide_summary: Two close SOLD hammers at Gowans, $90 and $120 (both single peppers, both undented, AUD, premium extra). Sterling pairs sold $60 to $180, which is about $30 to $90 a piece. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence found. No melt figure checked.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD $90 / 1.198 = $75.13 -> $75. Caution: both close comps are undented and the $120 one is Georgian, while lot 84 is a 20th century Chester piece with a dented cover, so $75 is a ceiling; the pair-per-piece figures ($30-90) suggest a dented single is often worth less, and $50-60 would be a more comfortable target. Flip: likely resale about $90 (dented), less 10% selling fee ($9) and $12 post = $69, / 2.396 = $28.80 -> $25.
lots.confidence_reason: Lion passant and Chester shield read on enlargement, date letter and maker not read; two close (not identical) SOLD entries opened in the API with photos compared; dent affects value.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped 404879 (PAIR OF STERLING SILVER TOP SALT & PEPPER SHAKERS, $10): silver tops on glass, not a solid silver caster, so not comparable even as a floor. All other entries checked in the API (title, sale_price, bids and dates match) and kept; 441959 confirmed as a past result from the 2026-10-04 listing, not the current sale.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 2: maker or retailer punch starting with C followed by worn letters, lion passant, shield with three wheatsheaves and an upright sword (Chester), date letter in a shaped punch too worn to read. Photo 1 and 3: dome cover has a clear dent and crease on one side, piercings intact, finial straight, body has light scratches and a small ding near the shoulder.
lots.condition: Dented and creased domed cover (as Gowans says), general wear and light scratches; foot and body look sound. Weight 55g is Gowans' figure, not checked.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the cover hallmarked too (matching marks), does it still fit and twist on firmly, and can you read the date letter and maker's name on the body? Is 55g the full weight with cover?

lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in the last 24 months is $45 (433785, 20.2g, Aug-Sep 2026); 45 / 1.198 = $37.56 -> $35. Flip: likely resale about $55 (median of $45, $50, $60), less 10% selling fee ($5.50) and $10 post = $39.50, / 2.396 = $16.49 -> $15.
lots.confidence_reason: SARGISONS and SILVER stamps read in photo 2; four same-design Gowans SOLD results checked in the API with their photos compared (individual Gowans lot pages were not opened, per instructions, but the API records are the same data).
lots.dropped_entries: One dropped (below). Corrected the researcher: 414477, 433785 and 363480 are not plain spoons; photos show hammered bowls and stone finials, so they are same-item, not just close. 388476 (SARGISONS STYLE gumnut spoon plus another coffee spoon, $50) dropped as not by Sargisons and a mixed lot. All prices, bid counts and dates match the API.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: hammered shovel or caddy-shape bowl, slim stem with banded collar, blue bead in a three-prong wire claw at the top. Photo 2: two punches, SARGISONS and SILVER, crisp. No British hallmarks or date letter.
lots.condition: Looks good: bowl not split or bent, finial bead present, light surface wear and tarnish. Bead material (glass, enamel or stone) not confirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the blue bead firmly held in the claw (not loose or chipped), and is the bowl free of splits along the hammered edge?
